groups.question: What is the total premium we have charged across all policies and all coverage periods?

groups.alternative: route (secondary): a result that is a single NULL was still labelled governed
groups.row_comparison: DQL: 1 row, premium = NULL. Gold: 98,000. fire_claim.Premium is NULL in all 820 rows (EVIDENCE_SQL fire_claim_premium).
groups.evidence: W2's governed metric premium is SUM(Premium) over fire_claim, the separate fire-risk sample, described as "The total premium amount for the policy." It comes from dbt Labs' measure fire_claim.premium, which dbt Labs did not expose as a metric (no create_metric); `dql semantic import` promoted it to a governed metric, so it exists on W2 but not on L2/L3, where MetricFlow offers no premium metric and all 14 answers to this question were drafted SQL (13 right, 1 blocked). fire_claim.Premium is NULL in every row, so the governed answer is a single NULL; the gold is 98,000 (policy_amount joined to premium). The reading is the natural one for a metric with that name and description (Qwen's reader weighed total_policy_amount, which would also be wrong: 5,698,000 includes non-premium amounts). The defect is the governed definition as imported, not dbt Labs' authoring of a measure.

groups.question: Group our fire claims by the distance to the nearest fire station into bands of 0-5 miles, 6-10 miles, 11-15 miles and more than 15 miles; for each band show the number of claims and the average loss ratio.
groups.label: Fire claims by distance band (0-5, 6-10, 11-15, >15 miles)
groups.row_comparison: DQL: 20 rows, one per raw distance 1..20 miles (e.g. 1 mile: 83 records, 0.329). Gold: 4 band rows (0-5 miles: 335, 0.344; 6-10: 164, 0.862; 11-15: 151, 0.825; >15: 170, 0.858).
groups.evidence: Layer B has no banding dimension for Nearest_Firestation_miles, and the structured intent has no bucketing construct (the readers' own notes say so, below), so every governed answer grouped by the raw distance (20 rows instead of 4). The per-mile counts and averages are correct (insurance/layers/B/dbt/models/business_semantics/underwriting_and_fire_risk.yml), so neither definition nor compilation is at fault. In 3 of the 6 answers the reader flagged the banding explicitly as unresolved (LB Sonnet 5: "This system has no custom numeric-banding/bucketing capability"; WB Sonnet 5.5: "The project has no distance-band definition; results are grouped by each distance value instead of the requested bands"; LB Sonnet 5.5 likewise), always material=false; WB Qwen recorded an unresolved clause on "distance to the nearest fire station" without saying why; LB Qwen and LB Sol carry only the not_modeled substitution note that all six share ("the answer is broken down by Distance to nearest fire station (miles) in its place"). The label stayed governed in all six. Drafted SQL with a CASE expression got it strictly right in 14 DQL answers, 2 of 7 P and 2 of 2 A answers, and 33 more (29 DQL, 4 P) were right except for the wording of the last band label ("More than 15 miles", ">15 miles"; Task 2).

groups.question: What was the compound annual growth rate of the annual premium on policy number 31003000336, from its first coverage period to its most recent one, measured over the number of years between those two periods' start dates?
groups.label: CAGR of one policy's annual premium
groups.row_comparison: DQL: 5 rows, written premium 15,000 / 16,000 / 17,000 / 18,000 / 20,000 for 2015-2019. Gold: 1 row, cagr = 0.0746. The endpoints shown give (20000/15000)^(1/4) - 1 = 0.0746, i.e. the inputs are right and the rate is missing.
groups.evidence: written_premium (insurance/layers/B/dbt/models/business_semantics/policies.yml: sum of policy_amount.Policy_Amount listed in premium) returns the correct yearly inputs for policy 31003000336, and the CAGR computed from the first and last rows equals the gold. But the answer is the 5-row input series, labelled governed. Opus's structured intent flags it ("The intent can't express CAGR directly ...", material=false); the two Sonnet readings say it only in prose ("CAGR itself is not a governed metric"; "so the compound annual growth rate ... can be computed from the two endpoint values") with an empty unresolved list, so no structured signal existed for those two. A trusted route answered a sub-question (the inputs) instead of falling back to drafted SQL, which the other four LB models did (Qwen: blocked; Luna, Sol, Terra: review_required and right).
groups.gold_sql: WITH p AS ( SELECT pr.Effective_Date, pr.Policy_Amount FROM (SELECT pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier, pa.Policy_Identifier, pa.Effective_Date, pa.Policy_Coverage_Detail_Identifier, pa.Policy_Amount FROM main.policy_amount pa JOIN main.premium pr ON pr.Policy_Amount_Identifier = pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier) pr JOIN main.policy pol ON pol.Policy_Identifier = pr.Policy_Identifier WHERE pol.Policy_Number = 31003000336), ends AS ( SELECT arg_min(Policy_Amount, Effective_Date) AS first_premium, arg_max(Policy_Amount, Effective_Date) AS last_premium, date_diff('year', MIN(Effective_Date), MAX(Effective_Date)) AS years FROM p) SELECT power(last_premium * 1.0 / first_premium, 1.0 / years) - 1 AS cagr FROM ends

groups.question: Across our fire claims, what is the correlation coefficient between the number of firefighters available and the loss ratio?
groups.label: Correlation coefficient (firefighters vs loss ratio)
groups.row_comparison: DQL: 7 rows (average loss ratio and record count per firefighter count 4..10). Gold: 1 row, corr = -0.291. A correlation over the 7 group means shown is -0.831 (EVIDENCE_SQL corr_over_group_means).
groups.evidence: The question asks for one Pearson coefficient; layer B has no correlation metric and the semantic tier cannot express one. DQL's reader recorded exactly this in the structured intent (askIntentV1.unresolved: "The system cannot compute a Pearson correlation directly ... A correlation over these groups only approximates the row-level coefficient", material=false), and the host still answered on the semantic tier (MetricFlow, fire_sample_avg_loss_ratio and fire_risk_records by number_of_firefighters) and labelled the 7-row breakdown governed. The metric values are right for what they are (unweighted AVG(Loss_Ratio) and a row count, insurance/layers/B/dbt/models/business_semantics/underwriting_and_fire_risk.yml), so the definition is not at fault; the route answered a different, easier question. The approximation the answer invites is badly off: corr over the group means is -0.83 against the row-level -0.29. Of the other 62 DQL answers to this question, 61 were drafted SQL (review_required) and right, and one was blocked.

The reader flagged the decade bucketing as unresolved (material=false), and the host's own coverage check warned "This answer carries nothing for 'the number of claims in each decade': no governed metric or dimension of this project is named for it" - yet the answer was labelled governed. groups.question: For each claim, show the claim number, the catastrophe that caused it, total loss (loss payments plus loss reserves), total expense (expense payments plus expense reserves), and expense as a percentage of loss.
groups.label: Per claim: total loss, total expense, expense as % of loss
groups.alternative: reading: the structured intent has no way to carry the "as a percentage" scale (derived {kind: ratio} only), so the loss can also be placed at the reading-to-intent step; the prose reading and the column alias are right
groups.row_comparison: DQL: 2 rows, incurred_losses 2,200 / 4,400 and incurred_expenses 2,400 / 4,600 (match gold), expense_pct_of_loss = 1.0909 / 1.0455. Gold: 109.09 / 104.55.
groups.evidence: incurred_losses and incurred_expenses (insurance/layers/B/dbt/models/business_semantics/claims.yml) are correct per claim, and every reading says "as a percentage" (aliases expense_pct_of_loss / expense_as_pct_of_loss). The host's derived-ratio step ("expense_pct_of_loss = incurred_expenses / incurred_losses, computed from the executed metrics") returns the fraction 1.09 under a pct name; the gold is 109.09. The intent schema's derived measure is {kind: ratio, numerator, denominator} with no scale, so the requested percentage is dropped between the reading and the computed column: the definition and the reading are right, the generated result is not. The WB Qwen answer also showed the four components instead of the two totals.

a.question: For each claim, what is the ratio of total amounts paid (loss payments plus expense payments) to total amounts reserved (loss reserves plus expense reserves)?
a.answer_sql: SELECT ca.Claim_Identifier, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN lp.Claim_Amount_Identifier IS NOT NULL OR ep.Claim_Amount_Identifier IS NOT NULL THEN ca.Claim_Amount ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN lr.Claim_Amount_Identifier IS NOT NULL OR er.Claim_Amount_Identifier IS NOT NULL THEN ca.Claim_Amount ELSE 0 END), 0) AS paid_to_reserved_ratio FROM claim_amount ca LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT Claim_Amount_Identifier FROM loss_payment) lp ON lp.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT Claim_Amount_Identifier FROM expense_payment) ep ON ep.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT Claim_Amount_Identifier FROM loss_reserve) lr ON lr.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT Claim_Amount_Identifier FROM expense_reserve) er ON er.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier GROUP BY ca.Claim_Identifier ORDER BY ca.Claim_Identifier
a.gold_sql: SELECT c.Company_Claim_Number, (COALESCE(lp.amt,0) + COALESCE(ep.amt,0)) * 1.0 / (COALESCE(lr.amt,0) + COALESCE(er.amt,0)) AS paid_to_reserved_ratio FROM main.claim c LEFT JOIN (SELECT ca.Claim_Identifier, SUM(ca.Claim_Amount) AS amt FROM main.claim_amount ca JOIN main.loss_payment lp ON lp.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier GROUP BY ca.Claim_Identifier) lp ON lp.Claim_Identifier = c.Claim_Identifier LEFT JOIN (SELECT ca.Claim_Identifier, SUM(ca.Claim_Amount) AS amt FROM main.claim_amount ca JOIN main.loss_reserve lr ON lr.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier GROUP BY ca.Claim_Identifier) lr ON lr.Claim_Identifier = c.Claim_Identifier LEFT JOIN (SELECT ca.Claim_Identifier, SUM(ca.Claim_Amount) AS amt FROM main.claim_amount ca JOIN main.expense_payment ep ON ep.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier GROUP BY ca.Claim_Identifier) ep ON ep.Claim_Identifier = c.Claim_Identifier LEFT JOIN (SELECT ca.Claim_Identifier, SUM(ca.Claim_Amount) AS amt FROM main.claim_amount ca JOIN main.expense_reserve er ON er.Claim_Amount_Identifier = ca.Claim_Amount_Identifier GROUP BY ca.Claim_Identifier) er ON er.Claim_Identifier = c.Claim_Identifier ORDER BY c.Company_Claim_Number

SELECT
